artworks.title: Title Page to Ovid's Metamorphosis, translated by G. Sandy
artworks.description: This is a detailed title page for "Ovid's Metamorphosis." The image includes various figures and symbolic elements arranged around the central text "Ovid's Metamorphosis Englished by G. S. Imprinted at London MDCXXVI Cum Privilegio." In the central area, two female figures in classical attire stand on either side of the text. Various figures with attributes are depicted beneath them, including a lyre and symbols of authority. A dynamic depiction of a charioteer riding through clouds is shown above with the text "AD AETHERA VIRTUS." Below the central text are symbolic representations labeled "AMORE" and "SAPIENTIA." The drawing features intricate engravings, classical motifs, and ornate borders.

artworks.title: Achmet I, Sultan of Turkey
artworks.description: The image is an engraved portrait of a man facing forward. He wears an Ottoman-style tall hat with a crescent motif and an ornate robe with fur trim. The portrait is surrounded by an ornate oval frame with decorative elements and an inscription that includes the name "ACOMATH" and Ottoman family titles.

artworks.title: Lancelot Andrewes, Bishop of Winchester
artworks.description: The image shows the upper body of a man facing slightly to his left, looking towards a book he is holding. He has pronounced facial features, a high forehead, defined eyebrows, and a connected mustache and beard. He wears a flat cap, formal clothing, and holds an open book in his left hand while pointing to a page with his right hand. There is a decorative oval frame in the background with a fine cross-hatching pattern, an inscription below the portrait identifying him as "The right reverend Father in God Lancelot, Bishop of Winchester, and Prælate of the Garter," and a coat of arms.

artworks.title: John Carter
artworks.description: The engraving depicts a man seated at a table with his head turned slightly to the left and tilted upwards. He has a pointed nose, thin lips, a beard, mustache, high forehead, receding hair, and neatly combed back hair. The man wears a dark, formal garment with a ruff collar. On the table in front of him are an inkpot with a quill, an open book, and an hourglass. The background has a dark, patterned texture, and there is Latin text at the top and bottom of the image.

artworks.title: Sir George Croke
artworks.description: The image shows an engraved portrait of a man's upper body. He is positioned at a slight angle, facing slightly to the left, with his hands visible, one of which appears to be holding a cylindrical object resembling a scroll. His facial features include prominent cheekbones, a faintly furrowed brow, and a serious expression. He has thin, wispy hair, slicked back, and a short, full beard with a thread of white. The man is wearing a fur-trimmed robe with a large, ornate ruff around his neck. Surrounding the oval-framed portrait is a decorative pattern of ribbons and banners showcasing Latin text. Below the portrait is a crest set on top of books. The background features intricate line patterns, focusing attention on the detailed depiction of the man’s face and attire.

artworks.title: George Clifford, Third Earl of Cumberland
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man from the waist up. He is facing forward with his head turned slightly to the right. The man has long, slightly wavy hair that falls on his shoulders and a styled goatee. His facial features include sharp eyebrows, deep-set eyes, a straight nose, and thin lips. He is dressed in ornate armor with intricate patterns and a detailed collar, a patterned sash over his shoulder, holding a staff in his right hand. He wears a medallion around his neck. The background has a decorative border with scrolls and inscriptions, two figures with swords, a coat of arms with Latin inscriptions, and an angel-like figure at the bottom.

artworks.title: George Clifford, Earl of Cumberland
artworks.description: The image depicts an engraved portrait of a man shown from the mid-torso upwards, positioned facing the viewer with his head slightly turned to his right. He has a long, pointed beard, a mustache, and wavy, shoulder-length hair. He wears ornate period clothing, a ruffled lace collar, a patterned garment, a sash, and holds a long staff or baton in his right hand. He wears a large chain around his neck with a decorative pendant. The portrait is surrounded by an ornate frame with heraldic symbols, banners, and two figures on each side. In the background above the frame are decorative motifs, including a coat of arms, and below the portrait is an inscription about the person depicted.

artworks.title: Sir Francis Drake
artworks.description: This image is a portrait of a man displayed from the waist up. He is seated in a slightly turned position, with his face turned towards the viewer. The man has short, curly hair that is slightly lighter in color and a pointed moustache and beard. He is dressed in a richly detailed garment, which includes a high collar with intricate patterns and a draped sash. One hand is resting on a globe, and he is holding a nautical staff. Behind him, there is a coat of arms. Below the portrait, there is an inscription composed of several lines of text. The background features wavy horizontal lines, and navigational tools such as an armillary sphere are visible on a table beside him.

artworks.title: Sir Francis Drake
artworks.description: This image depicts a man in a half-length portrait, facing slightly to the right with his head turned towards the viewer. He has distinct facial features, including a neatly trimmed mustache and beard, curly styled hair pushed back, and a receding hairline. The man is wearing a historical garment with intricate layering, a ruffled collar, and cuffs. He has a cloth over one shoulder, holding a staff or rolled paper in one hand and resting his fingers on a globe in the other hand. To his right, there are navigational tools such as a compass bowl and a small globe. Above him, a coat of arms displays two Latin phrases: "CXVXILIO. DIVINO" and "SIC PARVIS. MAGNA." The background features detailed linear patterns, emphasizing the subject and associated symbols.

artworks.title: James, Second Marquis of Hamilton
artworks.description: The image shows an engraving of a man in an ornate oval frame. The man has a pointed mustache, a short beard, and styled hair reaching his collar. He wears an embroidered outfit with a high lace ruff around the neck, typical of nobility. The outfit is detailed with patterns and floral motifs, along with decorative elements. There are no visible objects or jewelry. The background includes draped fabric and decorative designs within the oval frame. Latin text surrounds the frame, with an inscription at the bottom detailing the person's identity and titles.

artworks.title: Thomas Hilde, Puritan Divine
artworks.description: The image is a half-length portrait of a man seated with his body slightly angled to the side. He has a rounded face with neatly trimmed facial hair, prominent eyebrows, and wears a cap. His hair is wavy and of medium length. He is dressed in period-appropriate attire with a dark, intricately patterned robe, a white collared shirt, and a decorative bow tied at the throat. The man holds a rolled piece of paper or scroll in one hand. On the table in front of him are an inkpot with a quill, stacks of papers, and a rectangular object. The background is a draped fabric.

artworks.title: James I
artworks.description: The image is an engraving depicting the upper half of a man's body. He is seated, facing forward with a slight tilt to his left. The man has a mature face with a neatly trimmed beard and mustache, and his hair is mostly hidden beneath a crown adorned with detailing. He wears an elaborate, heavily embroidered robe with wide sleeves, adorned with a decorative collar and chain of office. In his right hand, he holds a scepter, while his left hand rests on an orb. The background features a patterned tapestry and the Latin words "BEATI PACIFICI" are visible above his head. The bottom of the image contains an inscription with a poetic verse.

artworks.title: Ben Jonson
artworks.description: The image shows the upper body of a man in an oval frame. He has a serious expression, with curly hair adorned with a laurel wreath. The man wears a buttoned garment with a high collar, and his hands are visible with an object in them. In the background, there are parallel hatching lines for depth. Text above and below the figure, with poetic text below. There are stacks of books on either side of the man.

artworks.title: Samson Lennard
artworks.description: The image shows a man seated, facing forward. He has deep-set eyes, a straight nose, a pointed beard, and wavy hair combed back from his forehead. He wears elaborate period clothing with a high lace collar and a richly decorated doublet. The man holds a small book in his left hand and a scroll in his right hand. The background displays thick drapery with embellishments and ornate crests on each side of the oval frame encircling the portrait.

artworks.title: Samson Lennard
artworks.description: The image is an engraving of a man seated and facing slightly to his left. He has a long goatee and short, swept-back hair. He wears an ornate doublet and ruffled collar, and holds an open book in his left hand. An oval frame surrounds him with Latin text. The background shows fabric drapery, a heraldic shield with fleur-de-lis patterns, and decorative scrollwork with a flower.

artworks.title: William Lilly
artworks.description: The image depicts a man seated at a table with his hand resting on a piece of paper and holding an open book. The man has a mustache, pointed goatee, wavy hair, and wears a buttoned-up jacket over a collared shirt. Near his hand is an ink stand with writing utensils. The background features an intricate design with stars, zodiac symbols, a crescent moon, and the sun.

artworks.title: Sir Thomas Lyttleton, Lawyer
artworks.description: The figure is shown from the upper body to the knees, positioned in a kneeling posture with both hands raised. The person has a distinct facial profile featuring a high forehead, a sharp nose, and a small mouth. Their head is covered by a cap or hood, with neatly trimmed facial hair. The attire consists of a luxurious robe with a high fur collar and fur-trimmed sleeves. An ornate lectern or stand is positioned in front of the person, supporting an open book with visible text written in a decorative script. A speech scroll emanates from the person's mouth, bearing the words "Ung Dieu et Ung Roy." In the background, heavy draped curtains frame the scene, and the floor is tiled with alternating light and dark squares.

artworks.title: Henry de Vere, Eighteenth Earl of Oxford
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man facing forward from the waist up. He is turned slightly to his left, with finely etched facial features including a prominent nose and wavy hair down to his shoulders. He is wearing nobleman attire, including a richly decorated doublet and a high, ruffled lace collar. In his left hand, he holds a long rod or staff. The frame around the portrait contains decorative scrollwork with text, and the background features engravings, banners, and a coat of arms.

artworks.title: Robert de Vere, Earl of Oxford
artworks.description: This image is an engraving of a man with a mustache and goatee, wearing armor and a sash diagonally across his chest. He has wavy hair and a detailed expression while looking at the viewer. The background is filled with decorative elements, including heraldic symbols at the top corners and text framing the portrait. There is also text at the bottom.

artworks.title: Philip II, King of Spain
artworks.description: The image shows a man with a mustache and beard, wearing a ruffled collar and detailed armor. He is positioned forward with a slight turn to the right. He wears a chain with a medallion around his neck. The background features a cross-hatched pattern within an oval frame. The border around the oval is thick. Text beneath the image identifies the person as "Philip the Second King of Spaine, Prince of the Low-countries," with the engraver's name "Ro. Vaughan sculp."

artworks.title: Sir Walter Raleigh
artworks.artist: Robert Vaughan after Simon de Passe
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of an individual's upper body. The person is facing forward with a slight turn to the side, holding a staff. They have facial features including a prominent forehead, large eyes, and a well-kept mustache and beard. The person has short, curly hair. The clothing is elaborate with a ruffled collar and ornate patterned fabric. An emblem is visible on the chest. In the background, there is patterned drapery, a shield with a zigzag design, and books. Below the image is scripted text identifying the person as Sir Walter Raleigh.

artworks.title: Sir Walter Raleigh
artworks.artist: Robert Vaughan after Simon de Passe
artworks.description: The image shows a man's upper body facing slightly left but looking directly at the viewer. He has a high forehead, arched eyebrows, prominent eyes, and short curly hair. The man has facial hair, including a mustache and pointed beard. He wears an elaborate garment with a ruffled collar, ornate embroidery, and buttons. His left hand holds a globe with a clamp over one of its supports. In the background are a curtain with a tassel, a shield with arrows on his left, and a stack of books on a shelf to the right. The scene is depicted as an engraving, focusing on his clothing and facial features.

artworks.title: Sir Walter Raleigh
artworks.artist: Robert Vaughan after Simon de Passe
artworks.description: The image shows an engraving of a man identified as Sir Walter Raleigh. He is portrayed seated, facing the viewer with his shoulders slightly angled. The man has distinct facial features, including deep-set eyes, a neatly trimmed mustache, and a pointed beard. His hair is wavy and styled back off his forehead. He is dressed in ornate Elizabethan clothing, featuring a patterned doublet and a large ruffled collar. He holds a stick in his right hand. There is a decorative piece around his neck that resembles a jeweled ornament. The background includes draped curtains on the top, a shield with a heraldic design on the left, and a bookshelf with several books on the right. Captions above and below the portrait indicate his identity as Sir Walter Raleigh.

artworks.title: Sir Walter Raleigh
artworks.artist: Robert Vaughan after Simon de Passe
artworks.description: The image displays a historical portrait of a man. He is positioned slightly angled to the viewer's right but looking directly at the viewer. The man has wavy, short hair and a prominent mustache and beard. He wears an elaborate ruffled collar and a richly detailed coat with ornate patterns and embellishments. His right hand is visible, holding a staff or cane. The background features intricate details, including a ship on a globe to his lower left and an array of books on shelves to his upper right. Above him is a decorative banner with the Latin inscription "Tam Marti, Quam Mercurio." The text at the bottom of the image identifies him as Sir Walter Raleigh, with the artist's signature, "Ro: Vaughan sculp," engraved beneath.
